9-3. Retired Regular Army Warrant Officers
This Accessions option allows Regular Army Warrant Officer retirees who meet the
minimum DA WO MOS proponent requirements, and suitability requirements to join the
ARNG. Although a RA WO may start the process prior to release from active duty
(REFRAD), they must be released from active duty and placed on the retired list to be
eligible for appointment in the ARNG. See PPOM 21-056 for more information.
  a. Basic eligibility RA Retired Warrant Officer. There is no established timeframe
for when a Retired RA Warrant Officer can request accession into the ARNG. To be
eligible for accession applicants must:
  (1) Possess a valid WO MOS (authorized to access in existing MOS only).
  (2) Meet eligibility standards for Warrant Officer IAW in AR 601-210, NGR 600-
101, and AR 611-110.
  (3) Meet Chapter 2 Commissioning Physical and Flight Physical (Chapter 4,
Class I) medical standards.
  (4) Meet the mental and conduct requirements outlined in NGR 600-101 and AR
40-501.
  (5) Attain minimum of a Secret security clearance or be able to attain Top Secret
if required for qualification in the WO MOS.
  b. Personnel management of RA Retired Warrant Officer.
  (1) The ROCC/State WOSM will verify the eligibility of the RA Soldier by
reviewing PS administrative documents.
  (2) The ROCC/State WOSM will complete the HRR Form 207A form and forward
to the State Command Chief Warrant Officer (CCWO) for certification.
  (3) The State CCWO will obtain TAG approval utilizing the HRR Form 207A. The
HRR Form 207A replaces the requirement for a Memorandum of Acceptance (MOA).

  62

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

  (4) The WOSM will work with the State Officer Personnel Management (OPM) for
Federal recognition and will ensure the initial VA Form 21-8951-2 or DA Form 7894 are
completed and signed before final accession.
  (5) Service Obligation. Upon accession, the service member will incur a 2-year
contractual obligation. This service obligation may be waived by the State TAG.

Note: Applicants are responsible for submitting the proper forms (VA Form 21-8951-2 or
DA Form 7894) to the Department of Veteran's Affairs (VA) and ensuring annual review
is completed (to include uploading into IPERMS).

9-4. Reserve Officers’ Training Corps/Simultaneous Membership Program (SMP)
The Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (ROTC) SMP is a voluntary officer-training
program designed to increase the number of ROTC officers available for Reserve
Forces Duty. Applicants will meet eligibility requirements listed in USACC Regulation
145-1. All 09R applicants must complete a chapter 2 MEPS physical, have a validated
checklist (HRR Form 200), control number via RZ workflow and review from ARNG-
HRR-O-ASO before REQUEST reservation and enlistment. SMP applicants are divided
into two categories, Potential SMP and Contracted Cadet/SMP.
  a. Eligibility (NPS/ PS). A Potential SMP (09R1) is an individual who is not
contracted with ROTC or enrolled in the advanced course (Military Science (MS) III and
IV) and have executed NGB Form 594-1. These applicants will:
  (1) Be a US Citizen, LPR, or US National, to include persons born in American
Samoa or the Swain Island.
  (2) Meet the age requirement for enlistment.
  (3) Have AFQT of 31 or higher.
  (4) Applicants who require a SR, a civil conviction waiver, or administrative
waiver for separations are not authorized to access until granted approval.
  (5) Meet medical fitness standards as outlined in DoDI 6130.03, Vol 1.
  (6) Be enrolled in a full-time regular course of instruction leading to a
baccalaureate or advanced degree at an eligible institution hosting or having a cross-
enrollment agreement or extension center agreement with another institution hosting an
Army ROTC program.
  (7) High school seniors are not eligible for SMP enlistment option. Exceptions
may be granted by ARNG-HRR-O-ASO for high school Minuteman nominees and
GRFD scholarship recipients, including TAG/CASA Minuteman nomination letter or
GRFD award letter in the exception request.
  (8) Be enrolled as MS I or II or enroll in MS I or MS II upon start of college.
College juniors beginning ROTC must be enrolled in MS III.
  b. Processing:
  (1) Applicants who have initialed NGB Form 594-1, Section II, “I am required to
complete basic training prior to enrollment in advanced ROTC course.” This option will
only be allowed for applicants whose states require Army Basic Combat Training in order
to access state tuition assistance. If the state does not require BCT, the 594-1 will be
amended per the following paragraph. Basic training will be pulled or the first available
RECSTA that aligns with the applicant’s academic schedule.

  63

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

  (a) MEPS GC will contact the ROC to pull reservation requiring BCT. Applicant
will be holding a skill level 1 vacancy in REQUEST 3.0 built as 09R1O00YY.
  (b) Applicants who enlist under this option must become a contracted Cadet
and supply a NGB Form 597-3 or a GRFD control number showing they have received
and accepted a scholarship.
  (2) Applicants who have initialed NGB Form 594-1, Section II, “I am not required
to complete basic training prior to enrollment in Advanced ROTC Course,” will not be
required to attend Basic Training prior to becoming a contracted cadet with the following
requirements.
  (3) Applicant must provide either a DA Form 597-3 showing they are a contracted
cadet or a GRFD control number showing they have received and accepted a
scholarship.
  (a) MEPS GCs will contact the ROC to pull reservation not requiring BCT.
Applicant will be holding a skill level 2 vacancy in REQUEST 3.0 built as 09R2O00YY.
Applicant will be built as 09R1O00YY on the 680-ADP page in IKROme. After the
reservation is pulled GC will update the OPAT scores, enlist confirm and ship confirm.
If ship confirm is not allowed, GC must submit JPAS ship workflow to ASO. Once that is
complete, the GC should be able to ship confirm.
  (b) MEPS GC will add one of the following comments on the DD Form 1966
Remarks section annotating the type of 09R1 enlistment based on para 3b above either
(1) or (2) based on applicant/RRNCO intent on day of enlistment.
  c. Exceptions to policy referencing 09R1 may be granted by ARNG-HRR-O-ROC.
ETPs must include a DA Form 4187 with any substantiating documentation. The
documents must include a memorandum from the PMS from the ROTC department the
09R1 is participating with.
  d. Eligibility (NPS/PS). A Contracted Cadet/SMP (09R2) is an individual who is
contracted with ROTC and has executed NGB Form 594-1 and DA Form 597 or 597-3.
These applicants will:
  (1) Be a US Citizen, LPR, or US National, to include persons born in American
Samoa or the Swain Island.
  (2) Meet the age requirement for enlistment.
  (3) Have an AFQT of 31 or higher.
  (4) Applicants who require an SR a civil conviction waiver, or administrative
waiver are not authorized to access until approved.
  (5) Meet medical fitness standards as outlined in DoDI 6130.03, Vo1.
  (6) Enlistment requires an approved JPAS ship workflow to clear the JPAS
submission in "Manage Investigation" to allow the MEPS GC to ship confirm REQUEST.
  e. Personnel management of 09R applicants.
  (1) PS applicants will enlist for a minimum term of service of 4 years. NPS
applicants will enlist for an 8-year term of service (minimum 4 x 4 option).
  (2) SMP participants will be assigned as an officer trainee in a unit based on
current or projected commissioned officer vacancies.
  f. Soldiers who voluntarily withdraw from or are involuntarily removed from SMP
must enter IET within 180 days of the effective date of the ROTC disenrollment memo.
These Soldiers are required to complete their remaining service obligation. Soldiers

  64

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

who refuse to attend or cannot be DMOSQ within 24 months of enlistment date will be
immediately discharged.

9-5. Foreign Language Recruiting Initiative (FLRI) 09C enlistment option
The FLRI 09C enlistment option is authorized for all ARNG RRBs. To fully maximize the
FLRI and its utility to the ARNG, it will be open to anyone for whom English is a second
language.
  a. Authorization FLRI enlistments are authorized in all four quarters of the fiscal year
(may be closed at any point in the FY due to overall CAT IV percentage).
  b. Eligibility.
  (1) Be a high school graduate.
  (2) Be a NPS applicant.
  (3) Attain an Armed Forces Qualification Test (AFQT) score of 21-30 with a
qualifying line score of 54 in the AO subtest. Applicants with a 31 AFQT or higher will
be enlisted for any program they qualify for, to include those applicants required to
attend English as a Second Language (ESL) training. If the individual took the High
School ASVAB, they must retest at the MEPS utilizing the iCAT ASVAB. Mobile
Examination Test (MET) Sites are not authorized for FLRI applicants.
  (4) Must take the TAPAS but are not required to achieve a passing score.
  (5) Achieve a score between 35 and 74 on the English Comprehension Language
Test (ECLT) or American Language Course Placement Test (ALCPT) at the MEPS.
ARNG-HRR-O-ASO can grant an ETP for up to 5 points to meet the minimum of 40
points on the ECLT. Applicants are not authorized to retake the ECLT to lower their
score to qualify for the FLRI program.
  (6) FLRI applicants will be informed of the following:
  (a) Soldier will not initially be guaranteed training in any specific MOS/CMF.
  (b) Soldier will not initially be guaranteed an assignment to any specific
station, unit, command, or area.
  (c) Soldiers will be required to attend the ESL Program at Lackland AFB, TX
for up to 30 weeks based on their current ECLT score.
  (7) All FLRI applicants whose primary language is not English will access as
MOS 09C1L00YY and in-process with the Reception Battalion at Fort Sill, OK prior to
attending ESL at Lackland AFB, TX. The MEPS GC will ensure that all FLRI applicants
accessing under the FLRI option reflects RECBN at Fort Sill, OK.
  c. Personnel management upon ESL Program completion.
  (1) Soldiers will be administered the ECLT or the ALCPT upon completion of ESL
Program. Soldiers scoring 75 or greater will be required to take the Armed Forces
Classification Test (AFCT). If the Soldier fails to attain the required score of 75 or better
on the ECLT, the individual will be separated from the ARNG as an entry-level
separation, regardless of AFQT and aptitude area scores. Telephonic waivers to this
rule will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis by ARNG-HRR-O for Soldiers scoring 70-
74.
  (2) The resulting scores from the AFCT will become the scores-of-record from
which qualifications for training and enlistment programs will be determined. If an AFCT

  65

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

of at least 21 is not obtained with at least one qualifying aptitude area score, the Soldier
will be assigned an MOS and enlistment program based on their initial ASVAB score.
  (3) Soldiers failing to qualify for an MOS will be discharged.
  (4) Soldiers discharged from the FLRI program, regardless of reason, will not be
eligible to re-enter the FLRI program. These applicants will be considered GNPS.
  (5) RENOs will be managed through the LNO and coordinated with the RRB.

9-6. ARNG College First Enlistment Option
The Army National Guard College First (NGCF) enlistment option provides NPS
applicants with the opportunity to serve in the ARNG and complete up to 2 years of full-
time education. Applicants who enlist under this option may be stabilized for up to 24
months upon completion of IET and reporting DMOSQ to the unit of assignment.
  a. Application. This policy applies to NPS applicants only. This policy does not apply
to anyone enlisting under the 09S or 09R enlistment option. Warriors who have enlisted
and have not shipped to training are not authorized to RENO their contract for this option.
  b. Implementation.
  (1) Due to the stabilization element of the NGCF option, each State may elect to
not offer this option to eligible applicants.
  (2) TAG of each State is the ultimate authority for the development and
implementation of the State Strength Maintenance programs. States may elect not to
offer this option to eligible applicants. If a State elects to opt into the Enlistment Option,
they are responsible for publishing their own stabilization guidance.
  c. Eligibility. To be eligible for the NGCF enlistment option, applicants must:
  (1) Be a NPS HSSR, HSDG, or a HSDG equivalent.
  (2) Meet enlistment eligibility criteria as stated in AR 601-210 and current
FYARNG AOC.
  (3) Have an AFQT of 50 (CAT 1-IIIA) or higher on the ASVAB.
  (4) Enlist on a 6x2 or 8x0 contract.
  (5) Complete IET using the standard training path and report DMOSQ to the unit
of assignment (split or alternate training is not authorized).
  (6) Be accepted as a resident or online student (full-time) to a college or
university that is accredited by the US Department of Education within 180 days of
reporting DMOSQ.
  d. Processing.
  (1) RRNCO.
  (a) For applicants currently enrolled in a college or university, the HRR Form
901 is required and will be uploaded into RZ.
  (b) Applicants currently attending a resident or online college or university, an
HRR Form 901 is required along with a current transcript. These documents will be
uploaded into RZ.
  (c) Use the HRR Form 800 (College First Enlistment Option Statement of
Understanding (SOU)) to counsel applicants on all requirements.
  (2) MEPS GC.

  66

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

  (a) The MEPS GC will process applicants by selecting the code TH (College
First ARNG Duty) in the available recruiting test programs drop down box. Verify with
the ROC, which States have opted into the Enlistment Option.
  (b) Upon verification of a letter of acceptance, HRR Form 901 (if applicable)
and current college transcript (if applicable), the MEPS GC will ensure the following
comment is annotated on the DA Form 1966 remarks “I understand I am enlisting in the
College First Enlistment Option.”
  (c) The MEPS GC is responsible for explaining NGCF requirements and
benefits outlined in the HRR Form 800 (College First Enlistment Option Statement of
Understanding) Guard Annex. The completed form will be uploaded into the applicant's
record.
  (3) Systems Processing. States will manually track College First applicants.
ARNG/IPPS-A will provide coding requirements to accommodate these Soldiers in the
IPPS-A system. Any technical issues or questions can be directed to ARNG Human
Resources Personnel – Systems (ARNG-HRP-S).
  e. Restrictions. To maintain eligibility in the program, the Soldier must:
  (1) Remain an active participant in an ARNG unit, be in good standing, and not
currently suspended of favorable personnel action for any reason.
  (2) Not receive a grade point average (GPA) below 2.0 for any 2 consecutive
semesters.
  (3) Provide the assigned unit with an official transcript within 30 days of the end of
each semester. This will be used to validate full-time status and GPA.
  (4) Not be discharged or separate from the Selected Reserve.
  (5) Not fail two consecutive AFTs or two consecutive Body Fat screening.
  (6) If an NGCF Soldier elects to enter the Inactive National Guard (ING), the Soldier
will be removed from the NGCF program. The Soldier will not be eligible to continue the
NGCF upon return from the ING.
  f. Mobilization/activation.
  (1) Soldiers who volunteer for mobilization or State Active Duty (SAD), waive their
NGCF stabilization period.
  (2) Soldiers who enlist under the NGCF option may be mobilized at the
commander’s discretion for any Domestic Support of Civil Authorities (DSCA) mission.
The Soldier may be eligible to continue NGCF option upon completion of the mission.
  g. Incentives. NGCF applicants are eligible for ARNG incentives provided they meet
criteria outlined in the current ARNG Selected Reserve Incentive Program (SRIP).
  h. Tracking.
  (1) Transcripts/college enrollment verification letter are required and must be
provided to the company/battery/troop commander stating the Soldier is enrolled as a
full-time student before each semester. A full-time student is defined as enrolled in 12
or more credits per semester or 9 or more credits per quarter.
  (2) States are responsible for tracking the stabilization period of NGCF
enlistments and ensuring they meet the criteria to remain in a non-deployable status.
The stabilization start- and projected end-dates will be annotated. States will maintain a
roster of all NGCF Soldiers within their State to ensure these Soldiers are not included
on the mobilization lists during the stabilization period.

  67

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

  i. Removal process. If the Soldier fails to maintain eligibility for this option,
commanders will notify the Soldier in writing of the disqualifying reasons(s). The
memorandum will include the basis of disqualification and the effective date of removal.
A copy of the memorandum will be provided to the Soldier and uploaded into their
iPERMS. The effective date of removal will be recorded and tracked as outlined above.
The Soldier will be returned to the State and will no longer be under the College First
Enlistment Option. Soldiers who are scheduled for training and subsequently enroll in
college in which the semester begins prior to the ship date will be held to their ship date
and required to postpone their college start date.

9-7. ARNG Special Forces (18X) Enlistment Option
The ARNG Special Forces (18X) enlistment option provides NPS applicants with the
opportunity to enlist into the Special Forces training pipeline. Applicants who enlist
under this option will attend 11B OSUT and will return to their State Duty Military
Occupational Skill Qualified (DMOSQ) in the event they fail to complete Special Forces
training.
  a. Authorization. The 18X enlistment option is authorized for all ARNG RRBs with
force structure to support the enlistment.
  b. Eligibility. To be eligible for the 18X enlistment option, applicants must:
  (1) Be a US Citizen or LPR. If not a US Citizen by the beginning of the Special
Forces Qualification Course (SFQC), the applicant will be dropped from the 18X training
program.
  (2) Be 18 years of age by ship date to 11B OSUT and have not reached their
35th birthday.
  (3) Must enlist 6x2 or 8x0.
  (4) Acknowledge the requirement to attend the Basic Airborne Course.
  (5) Must have a minimum General Technical (GT) score of 110 and a minimum
Combat Operation score of 100. If applicant does not have the required score, then
they may take the AFCT/ASVAB to attempt to raise their line scores.
  (6) Be a high school graduate or higher. Exceptions for General Education
Development (GEDs) may be considered.
  (7) No derogatory or adverse information provided within the SF 86 which would
preclude the granting of a security clearance. Must be able to attain a Secret or Top-
Secret security clearance. Must obtain security clearance by the beginning of the
SFQC, or the applicant will be dropped from the 18X training program.
  (8) Medical fitness Standards.
  (a) Must have an approved Special Forces Physical prior to Special Forces
Assessment and Selection.
  (b) Female Soldiers must have a negative pregnancy test within 30 days of
Special Forces Assessment and Selection (SFAS) report date.
  (c) Have a physical profile rating of no less than 111221 and meet additional
requirements for vision in accordance with AR 40–501 or be willing to undergo refractive
eye surgery.
  (9) Be enlisted in pay grade E-2 or above (based on HQDA exception for this
option).

  68

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

  (10) Be able to swim 50 meters wearing boots and an Army Combat Uniform
(ACU) prior to graduating from the Special Forces Qualification Course.
  c. Processing.
  (1) The MEPS GC is responsible for explaining to the applicant they will be
required to serve the remainder of their commitment in their PMOS (11B) in the State of
entry into the ARNG if unable to complete Special Forces training to become CMF 18
DMOSQ.
  (2) The MEPS GC will ensure the orders reflect 18X. For further orders
processing guidance see the MEPS Processing PPOM.
  d. Incentives.18X applicants are eligible for ARNG incentives provided they meet
criteria outlined in the current ARNG Selected Reserve Incentive Program (SRIP)
guidance.

9-8. English as a Second Language (ESL)
(Subsumes and rescinds SMOM 25-013)
The ESL program for non-FLRI applicants is designed to improve an applicant’s
English-speaking ability. Applicants who do not meet FLRI criteria, and score between
35-74 on the ECLT and >31 AFQT on the ASVAB, will attend ESL training at Lackland
AFB. This is available for both NPS and PS applicants. Refer to AR 601-210
paragraph 5-1.
  a. Exceptions to policy will not be entertained for ECLT scores under (less than) 40.
  b. Applicants will be assigned an MOS they qualify for based on current ASVAB
(line scores) and is a primary “ARNG AUVS Top-Loaded vacancy” (but are not
authorized to enlist into an MOS or enlistment option that requires additional (specialty)
training (e.g., FSPP, 35M/35P (DEFLANG)) and/or an MOS requiring AIT length beyond
24 weeks.
  c. Warriors will in-process at Ft. Sill prior to attending ESL at Lackland AFB, TX.
The RFO will ensure orders associated with ESL reflecting Ft. Sill, OK as the Reception
Battalion (RECBN).
  d. Minimum “AO” score for ESL is not required.
  e. GCs will contact the ROC to pull ALL FLRI or ESL reservations.
  f. ESL attendance cannot be waived, once an applicant is administered the ECLT
and requires ESL training due to a score between 35-74, that score remains valid, and
they will require ESL.
  g. ECLT retest period is 30 days from initial test, 30 days from the second test, and
then a 6-month waiting period for the third test.
  h. Applicants who score 75 or higher on the ECLT are not authorized to retest to
score lower to qualify for FLRI.
  i. All applicants who have resided in the US for less than one year require the
ECLT prior to enlistment. The exception to use this policy is for applicants from
countries where English is the native language and English is the only language spoken
by the applicant (see Table 9-1 for native English-speaking countries).
  j. Applicants processing in Puerto Rico will only be required to take the ECLT if
they are demonstrating a language barrier or if they have scored below a 31 on the
ASVAB. Applicants from Puerto Rico will only be required to take the ECLT if they

  69

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

demonstrate a language barrier or if they score below a 31 on the ASVAB. Applicants
in Puerto Rico that score between a 21-30 on the ASVAB and between 35-74 on the
ECLT will enlist as 09C. Applicants from Puerto Rico that score between a 21-30 on the
ASVAB and 75 or higher on the ECLT, will enlist as 09M.
  k. Applicants who previously processed for enlistment in Puerto Rico and did not
meet the ECLT or AO requirement for FLRI, will still be required to have a passing
ECLT or AO score to process. This group has already demonstrated there is a
language barrier, an ASVAB retest with a 31 or higher would not qualify them for
enlistment, a passing ECLT or ECLT/AO if FLRI, would be required.
Applicants will be assigned to an MOS for which they qualify but are not authorized to
enlist in an MOS or enlistment option that requires additional or specialty training (e.g.
FSPC, Language Training, Airborne) , and/or an MOS requiring an AIT length beyond
24 weeks.

Appendix B. Certification Requirements for SELRES Members for the Purpose of

chunks.title: FY26 AOC: Appendix B: Certification Requirements for Naturalization
chunks.text:
Naturalization

B-1. In accordance with current DoD policy, OUSD memorandum, and PPOM
guidance, Soldiers are authorized to request certification of honorable service for
purposes of naturalization immediately upon entering Active Duty or attending drill with
their Selected Reserve unit. This includes those Warriors in the training pipeline
attached to the RSP.

B-2. The certification will be completed on the United States Citizenship and
Immigration Services (USCIS) Form N-426 and must be signed by a Certifying
Official who is O-6 / GS-15 or higher. A copy of the certification will be filed in the
Soldier’s Army Military Human Resource Record (AMHRR)/iPERMS. When certifying
the N-426 the Commander must select “Selected Reserve of the Ready Reserve”. Do
not select “Other” and type “National Guard”, as this will nullify the form. The date of
certification must be the date of the SECOND RSP drill or later. Dating the form the
date of the first RSP drill or earlier will nullify the form.

B-3. Authorized certifying officials must certify or deny a Soldier's certification request,
and return it to the Soldier, within 30 calendar days of submission. Commanders and
certifying officials may not decline to process or act on the request, or deny the request,
based on the Soldier’s time in service. Commanders and certifying officials are not
permitted to impose local restrictions or prerequisites, such as minimum training or
service requirements, as a condition of certifying honorable service.

  78

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

B-4. Soldiers should access the two required forms: N-400 and N-426 on the USCIS
website: https://www.uscis.gov/. To ensure the current USCIS form is being used,
always access the forms from the website. Never used preprinted forms. Using the
website search feature, enter each form number, save the form as a pdf file and
complete. Complete the forms neatly and accurately, then print and ink sign both forms.
Digital signatures are not authorized. Soldiers will submit the completed N-426 to their
Chain of Command for certification and processing. Only the N-426 requires the
Certifying Official's signature. The preferred method of sending the documents to
USCIS is to upload them through the USCIS "My Account" through the USCIS website.
Alternately, mail both forms together, along with a copy of the DD form 4 to the local
USCIS office. The address can be found by entering the Soldier's zip code in the
“Office Locator” on the USCIS website. If Soldiers or their Chain of Command have
questions about the process, they may be addressed by calling the USCIS Military Help
Line at 877-CIS-4MIL (877-247-4645, TTY: 800-877-8339) or DHS Email.

B-5. Common Errors Application / Petitions and Other Information
   a. When completing the N-400 prior to 1 full year of service, the Soldier should select
block “E” (Military Service During Period of Hostilities). Prior to 1 year service the
Soldier is not eligible for selection “F” (At Least One Year of Honorable Service at any
time). After 1 full year of service, the Soldier will select “E” and provide as evidence a
DD214 from the training base along with a completed N-400 and N-426. Selecting the
incorrect block will nullify the application.
   b. USCIS Account and Phone App. The Soldier should wait until the certified N-
426 is received to set up an account with USCIS. The USCIS “My Account” has a
30 day disable feature. If there is no activity in the account for 30 days, or an
active petition, the account will disable. Upload the completed USCIS forms N-400,
N-426 and a copy of the DD form 4 for processing. The USCIS "My Account" and the
USCIS App for both iPhone and Android phones will allow the Soldier to track the
progress of their petition and allows for secure messaging so the Soldier may
communicate rapidly and securely with their USCIS Case Manager. This is especially
useful when making corrections or answering questions USCIS has regarding their
petition. By interacting with the Case Manger, the Soldier can reduce the processing
time of their petition.
   c. Once the Soldier's petition for naturalization has been accepted and entered in the
USCIS system, the Soldier will receive a notification in the mail (USCIS form I-797) at
the physical address, in the email listed on the N-400 and in the “My Account”. To track
the progress of the Soldier's petition, the Soldier may enter their USCIS case number,
which is provided on the notice. The case number will be three letters followed by 10

  79

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

numbers. It is imperative that the Soldier frequently check for updates on the
petition and follow through with Requests for Evidence (RFE’s) from USCIS.
  d. If the Soldier changes address after filing their petition, or when shipping to
training the Soldier must send a message through their My Account (phone App or
computer) providing the new home address, or if to training a simple statement of “I’m
shipping to Basic Training on (date) at Fort (location)”. One of the main reasons for
extended processing times is lack of communication with the USCIS Case Manager.
Soldiers who fail to monitor their petition or follow through with RFE’s risk having
their petition denied for abandonment of the petition.

B-6. Processing for Naturalization while in the BCT training base. It is imperative the
RSP Sergeant prepare the Soldier for the process. Failing to do so shifts the work to
the Training Base Liaisons who do not have the time and manpower to assist the
number of Soldiers in this task.
  a. The N-400 is a lengthy document similar to an SF86 which many young Soldiers
need information from their parents to complete. For this reason, the N-400 should be
completed and saved in the Soldier’s USCIS My Account within 30 days of shipping to
BCT.
  b. If the Soldier is married and has children, copies of the marriage certificate and
children’s birth certificates should be uploaded in their USCIS account. By doing this
the documents do not need to be hand carried to training. If the Soldier has been
arrested, regardless of disposition, for Felony or Misdemeanor offenses copies of the
police and court records must also be uploaded in the USCIS account. Two Fingerprint
cards and a passport photo are also required. These can be hand carried to training or
obtained while in reception station.
  c. The N-426 can be obtained from the Chain of Command before shipping to BCT
and uploaded along with the N-400 and other documents. Alternately it can be obtained
through the training base Chain of Command. During training it will be sent to the
Commander for signature sometime towards the end of BCT. For OSUT Trainees the
USCIS virtual interview and Swear-in will be coordinated by the Army ATC personnel
and held during the AIT phase of training. For Soldiers changing installations for AIT the
Soldier MUST send a message in the USCIS My Account that he/she is moving to Fort
(location) on (Date). This assists USCIS in forwarding the Naturalization petition to the
office servicing the AIT training base for completion. The USCIS virtual interview and
Swear-in will be coordinated and held during AIT training.

B-7. LPR Soldiers who petition for expedited naturalization under this program and are
subsequently discharged with an Honorable characterization of service retain their
eligibility for naturalization. Under USCIS policy, all applicants must show that they

  80

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

have been or continue to be a person of good moral character (GMC). For military
personnel applying under expeditated naturalization, the period during which service
members or veterans must show GMC starts 1 to 5 years from the date of filing
(dependent upon military provision and status per USCIS policy). In all cases, the
applicant must also show that they continue to be a person of GMC until the time of
their naturalization. Applicants must understand that their conduct in the military and
outside of the military may impact their application and process for naturalization.
Previous policy treated uncharacterized entry-level discharges as “under honorable
conditions”; however, current policy is that a military member discharged with an entry-
level uncharacterized discharge after 1 August 2024 is not eligible for military
naturalization.

B-8. All LPR Warriors / Soldiers will be counseled on their ability to apply for expedited
naturalization as a service member. They will acknowledge the steps required of them
to apply, as well as other important information related to the naturalization process, on
DA Form 4856 (Developmental Counseling Form). The template for counseling
language is provided in Figure B-1 below.

B-9. Updating the Soldier’s records with Naturalization information. Soldiers that
become naturalized post-accession are required to provide a copy of the Naturalization
Certificate (USCIS form N-550) or Certificate of Citizenship (USCIS form N-560) for the
purpose of updating their personnel service and security records.
  a. If obtained prior to or during Advanced Individual Training (AIT), Soldiers will
provide a copy of their N-550 or N-560 to their Recruiter and RSP Leaders. The
document will be forwarded to the servicing Personnel Office (S1 / G1) to update the
Soldier’s citizenship information in IPPS-A and file the documents in the Soldier’s
AMHHR/iPERMS. The document will also be sent to the servicing S-2 / G-2 or the
ASO. The G-2 or ASO will send a copy to the Defense Counterintelligence and Security
Agency (DCSA) requesting an update to the background investigation and upgrade in
security clearance eligibility from “No Clearance Eligibility” to “Secret clearance”.
  b. If obtained after Advanced Individual Training (AIT), the document will be given to
the Unit Readiness NCO or S1, who will process accordingly to have the documents
filed in the Soldier’s AMHRR/iPERMS, citizenship updated in IPPS-A, and document
forwarded to S2/G2 channels for background investigation / clearance eligibility update
request through DSCA.

Appendix C. Background Investigation and Security Clearance Issues

chunks.title: FY26 AOC: Appendix C: Background Investigation and Security Clearance
chunks.text:
(Subsumes and rescinds SMOM 25-016)

C-1. RRNCOs, RRSCs, and MEPS GGs, and other personnel involved in the
enlistment process at both MEPS and remote processing will use the guidance below
regarding completion of the SF Form 86 and security process. All personnel in the
enlistment process will ensure the utmost attention to detail is applied when completing
the SF Form 86. DA PAM 611-21 is the qualification reference for all MOSs and for
additional MOS specific requirements not addressed in this guidance.

C-2. All applicants for enlistment will be processed for a new SF86 regardless of
whether they have a current investigation and clearance. A new investigation
submission is required for all enlistments. Recruiters and MEPS GCs must counsel all
applicants that it is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure their SF86 is complete and
accurate. Omissions of relevant facts or information from the SF86 is the same as lying
on the SF86. All applicants regardless of MOS and security clearance requirement
must be counseled that there is a potential that a Background Investigator contracted by
DCSA may call them as part of the investigation. It is the new Soldier’s responsibility to
respond to the Investigator by meeting if required and answering their questions.
Failure to respond will delay or stop the background investigation. If this occurs the
Soldier is not authorized to ship to training until the Tier 3 or Tier 5 investigation is back
in progress.

C-3. Security Interview.
  a. Only four MOSs require a security screening performed by the ASO prior to
enlistment, as follows: 17C, 35N, 35P, and 35S. For these MOSs, the MEPS GC will
submit a suitability workflow for MOS Quals, indicate in the workflow “Security
Screening”, and list the MOS.
  b. Indicate whether the interview is at the MEPS or at an approved off-site location
(i.e., Recruiting Station, RRB). A valid government phone number must be provided;
the applicant’s home or cell phone will not be used for this purpose. The Screener must
be able to reach the number at the scheduled time and location.
  c. Prior to the interview, the MEPS GC will review the SF86 with the applicant to
ensure all questions are answered completely and correctly. Security Screeners will
review the packet prior to the interview and will make minor corrections. However. if
there are several issues, the workflow will be returned and the RRNCO and MEPS GC
will be required to make corrections to the SF86 prior to rescheduling a new interview.

C-4. Top Secret/SCI Clearance MOS Processing.
   a. Prior to shipping training for an MOS requiring a TS/SCI clearance, Warriors
must meet minimum clearance requirements IAW TRADOC Regulation 350-6, table 4-
3. Interim TS/SCI clearance packets are submitted to DCSA by the ARNG-HRR-O-
ASO after enlistment.
   b. Due to the processing time for a TS/SCI clearance, the following MOSs are
required to have a minimum of 60 days in the RSP before shipping: 17C, 35G, 35N,

  84

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

35P, and 35S. This includes anyone renegotiating their contract from a non-clearance
or Secret clearance MOS.
  c. Warriors may ship earlier than 60 days, but no earlier than 30 days from
enlistment for the following MOSs: 12Y, 17E, 35F, 35M, and 35T. Warriors
renegotiated from a non-clearance or Secret clearance MOS to one of these five MOSs
may ship under 30 days if they already have a Secret clearance granted in DISS. The
minimum security clearance requirement is an open T5 investigation with an interim
Secret clearance granted by the State Security Manager. The interim Secret clearance
must be posted in DISS. Training base Security Offices will not accept a memorandum
for interim clearance.
  d. Warriors denied an interim clearance for any TS/SCI MOS, may have their
training cancelled. If this occurs, the Warrior will be required to stay in the RSP until
DCSA has completed their T5 investigation and granted a TS/SCI clearance. They will
not be allowed to renegotiate or ship for any MOS, regardless of clearance level until
their clearance adjudication is determined.
  e. Due to interim clearance denial cases being very few, States should assume
TS/SCI MOS Warriors are clear to ship on their scheduled ship date. Any case that is
not clear will be communicated directly to the State by the ARNG-HRR-O-ASO, with
necessary actions.
  f. For TS/SCI MOSs, RRNCOs and MEPS GCs will check DA Pam 611-21 to
ensure Applicants meet all requirements of the MOS prior to processing. Ensure the
applicant provides details in RZ for all foreign travel, foreign connections, and financial
issues.

C-5. High-Risk Countries Policy.
  a. Applicants who have immediate family members (spouse, parents, siblings,
children, stepchildren, or cohabitant of the individual) who are citizens, dual citizens, or
reside in any of the countries listed below may not access into any of the MOSs with
High-Risk Countries restrictions. High-Risk Country restricted MOSs are as follows:
17C, 35N, 35P, 35S.
  b. DA PAM 611-21 refers to the High-Risk Countries, as determined by the National
Security Agency (NSA), as Foreign National Associations (FNAs). Exceptions will not
be considered.
  c. High-Risk Countries include Afghanistan, Belarus, China, Cuba, Iran, Iraq,
Lebanon, Libya, North Korea, Pakistan, Russia, Somalia, Syria, Ukraine, Venezuela,
and Yemen.

C-6. Enlistment Option 18X.
   a. Applicants for MOS 18X are disqualified if any of the following conditions to them:
  (1) Marijuana usage of more than five times.
  (2) Marijuana usage within 150 days of enlistment.
  (3) One time use of any other illicit drug or controlled substance without a
prescription at any time.
  (4) Two minor non-traffic convictions within five years of enlistment.

  85

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

  (5) One minor non-traffic conviction within five years of enlistment along with
three or more traffic convictions within 12 months of enlistment.
  (6) Conviction for an offense at the misconduct level IAW AR 601-210.
  (7) Intoxications; five or more within 12 months of enlistment. Defined as loss of
coordination, dizziness, staggering, or acting in a fashion that you would have been
embarrassed had you been sober.
  (8) Indebtedness: delinquent bills of $2,500 or more or in collection for $2,500 or
more where no payment plan has been established by the lender. Payment plans must
show a minimum of three consecutive monthly payments of the minimum amount due
on the payment plan.
  (9) Bankruptcy (any chapter) within five years of enlistment.
  b. The 18 Series Proponency is the approval authority for applicants with any
disqualifiers listed above. Submit suitability workflow to the Accessions Suitability Office
(ASO) for routing to the approval authority.

C-7. Career Management Field (CMF) 31 and CMF 37.
   a. Major Misconduct conviction IAW AR 601-210 paras 4-11 and 4-4, regardless of
the date of occurrence.
   b. DUI or DUI reduced to reckless driving where the fine is $500 or more, or if
confinement was ordered, regardless of the date of occurrence.
   c. Three or more minor traffic convictions within 12 months of enlistment or eight or
more traffic convictions in total (parking tickets excluded).

C-8. Enlistment Options 09S and 09W.
  a. The Accessions Suitability Office is the SR approval authority for the following.
  (1) Any offense with a fine of $500 or more, excluding court cost.
  (2) Any offense where confinement was ordered, regardless of suspended
sentence or deferred disposition.
  (3) Any offense that involves contributing to the delinquency of a minor, spousal
or child abuse, any sex-related crime, or any offense under chapter 4 that is listed as a
misconduct (300 level) offense
  b. Non-waiverable security clearance disqualifiers. The Officer Strength Manager or
Warrant Officer Strength Manager at the state level must screen applicants for any of
the following:
  (1) Indebtedness: delinquent bills of $2,500 or more or in collection for $2,500 or
more where no payment plan has been established by the lender. Payment plans must
show a minimum of three consecutive monthly payments of the minimum amount due
on the payment plan.
  (2) Bankruptcy (any chapter) within five years of enlistment.
  (3) More than six times Marijuana usage in the past 12 months.
  (4) One time use of any illegal drug of any kind other than marijuana, regardless
of the date of the usage.
  (5) Intoxications; five or more within 12 months of enlistment. Defined as loss of
coordination, dizziness, staggering, or acting in a fashion that you would have been
embarrassed had you been sober.

  86

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

C-9. Disqualifiers for MOSs 12Y, 17E, 35F, 35G, 35L, 35M, 35T, 89D
  a. An applicant formerly affiliated with the Peace Corps within the four years
preceding enlistment is not eligible. If affiliation was more than four years ago, enlistment
is allowed, no ETP required.
  b. Indebtedness: delinquent bills of $2,500 or more or in collection for $2,500 or more
where no payment plan has been established by the lender. Payment plans must show
a minimum of three consecutive monthly payments of the minimum amount due on the
payment plan.
  c. Bankruptcy (any chapter) within five years of enlistment.

C-10. Renegotiation from a non-clearance or secret clearance MOS into an MOS
requiring a TS/SCI clearance requires the Soldier to update all questionnaires in RZ, a
new SF86 to be regenerated, all four new signature pages dated the same date as the
new SF86, new fingerprints, and a T5 investigation submission. MEPS GCs should
contact the ASO if there are questions or if they are unable to submit the new
investigation.

Appendix D. Expedited Screening Protocol (ESP)

chunks.title: FY26 AOC: Appendix D: Expedited Screening Protocol (ESP)
chunks.text:
D-1. The ESP optimizes intelligence data sources and analytics to provide multi-point
identity and detection of allegiance, foreign preference and foreign influence,
counterintelligence, counterterrorism, and insider threat concerns not detected in
traditional vetting and background investigation processes. The ESP ensures all
military recruits and recently accessed military members are screened for allegiance to
the United States and ensures foreign preference and foreign influence concerns are
appropriately mitigated.

D-2. The SF 86 will be submitted to the National Background Investigation Bureau
(NBIB) for initiation of a background investigation. NBIB will filter the SF 86 for
individuals with potential risk indicators associated with allegiance, foreign influence,
and foreign preference per the criteria set forth in questions 9,10, 11, 12, 15.3, 17-20b,
25, or 29. All applicants with one or more Yes answers to the above noted questions
will be referred to the Expedited Screening Cell (ESC) for protocol processing in
conjunction with the background investigation. RRNCOs will ensure that all the
questions in RZ are answered completely and truthfully. The omission of any required
data could hinder the applicant’s background investigation, may cause a delay in
shipping to Initial Entry Training or the completion date, or may result in a fraudulent
enlistment discharge.

D-3. The ESC will process the pertinent SF 86 information through the ESP. The ESP
will produce one of two possible results: No Potential High-Risk Indicators or High-Risk
Indicators. High Risk Indicators will be separated into those that can be mitigated and
those that cannot be mitigated.

  87

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

  a. No Potential High-Risk Indicators: Are results that do not identify any potential
High-Risk Indicators, ESC personnel will annotate RZ accordingly with the favorable
result. The goal for completion is within 14 days of the date on which the ESC received
the SF 86-QFNSP information. Warrior is authorized to continue preparation for training
or continue training if already shipped.
  b. Potential High-Risk Indicators are results that require further analysis to be
conducted to confirm identity and assess the level of risk (Mitigatable Risk or Un-
mitigatable Risk). Warriors will be held at their current duty station (RSP, BCT, or AIT)
and will not be allowed to move from their duty location until ARNG-HRR-O-ASO
receives an official notification indicating the Warrior has been favorably cleared by the
ESC or a decision has been rendered on unfavorable ESP results. If the ESC finds
mitigating information, they will clear the Warrior for continued processing. If the ESC
cannot find mitigating evidence, the ESC will make an unfavorable determination. The
goal for completion of analysis and potential mitigations is within 90 days of receipt of
SF 86-QFNSP data by the ESC.

D-4. If the ESC finds the Warrior to be unfavorable, Warrior will be discharged without
delay as outlined in Directive-Type Memorandum (DTM) 19-008 (with incorporating
changes) and AR 135-178.

Appendix E. Prior Service Record Management and Processing

chunks.title: FY26 AOC: Appendix E: Prior Service Record Management and Processing
chunks.text:
E-1. The ARNG Accessions Clerk at the National Records Center in St. Louis is
available to facilitate PS records requests that cannot be fulfilled by a State iPERMS
super-user. An applicant endorsed SF Form 180 is required and must be kept on file for
a minimum of three years. Submissions will be forwarded to the ARNG PS Records
Liaison, 1 Archives Drive, St. Louis, MO 63138.

E-2. Accessions Suitability Office
Personnel assigned to the Accessions Suitability Office have iPERMS super-user
access and can receive requests for records for all three Army components. To
facilitate quicker turnaround times for record requests, applicants will initiate and sign a
SF 180 prior to obtaining records required for accession. Please send the encrypted
email with the signed SF 180 to usarmy.knox.ngb.list.arng-accessions-suitability-
mgrs@army.mil. Once the SF 180 is received, ARNG-HRR-O-ASO will query iPERMS
for the requested documents and send them via email encrypted to the requestor.

E-3. Requesting Records From Other Services / Offices
   a. See SF 180, page 2, for address list of records custodians and self-service
websites for each military branch and other offices.
   b. If necessary, request records from the Army Criminal Investigative Division (CID).

  88

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

Appendix F. Pre-MEPS LiveScan Result Requirements

chunks.title: FY26 AOC: Appendix F: Pre-MEPS LiveScan Result Requirements
chunks.text:
(Subsumes and rescinds SMOM 25-017)

F-1. All States will submit fingerprints (FPs) electronically via LS devices utilizing Cross
Match ArcID at https://livescanrsn.usarec.army.mil/#. Fingerprint submissions are
required for all applicants, to include Prior Service Field Enlistments, Non-MEPS
Enlistments, and Direct Commissioning and Accessions.
  a. Fingerprint results are not required for ASVAB testing and MEPS physical.
Applicants who were not Live Scan fingerprinted and are projected to “Physical Only,”
an “X” projection, must have MEPS fingerprints submitted prior to leaving the MEPS.
Applicants who intend to enlist must be projected to enlist, an “A” projection, may enlist
if fingerprint results are complete.
  b. Applicants are authorized to non-MEPS enlist (IAW local MEPS GC SOP) once
fingerprint results are posted in RZ and the enlistment “A” projection is reviewed and
given a “Go Packet” in process checkpoint. Non-MEPS applicants must have fingerprint
results that are not older than 100 days from the closed date on the Case Closing
Transmittal.
  c. The HRR Form 369 must be completed when the initial appointment is
conducted. The recruiter should ask the applicant questions, mark the applicable
response, and sign digitally. Only the recruiter should sign the form, while the applicant
does not initial or sign it. Ink or a wet signature is not authorized.
  d. Applicants may continue to process without Live Scan results for the reasons
below. Exceptions will be considered by the Accessions Suitability Office via suitability
workflow. Applicants who were granted an exception to enlist without fingerprint results
will be discharged if an undisclosed 300 level or higher law violation returns on a RAP
Sheet, regardless of disposition. Retain is not authorized.
  e. Exceptions include:
  (1) Sustained Equipment failure
  (2) Sustained Network issues
  (3) Inclement weather
  (4) Safety concerns
  (5) Excessive travel distance
  f. To request an exception or for support contact the ASO at (502) 684-3241 or
(502) 684-3245 or for general questions email to usarmy.knox.ngb.mbx.arng-
accessions-suitability@army.mil or the MS TEAMS message to ASO with an attached
screen shot.

Note: Exceptions will not be approved while the applicant is at MEPS.

F-2. In the event of national LS outage, ARNG-HRR-O-ASO will obtain permission from
HQDA to process applicants on a temporary basis without LS results. A REQUEST
Flash message will be published immediately with all instructions.

F-3. Live Scan may not be submitted more than 30 days prior to the applicant turning
17.

  89

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

F-4. Live Scan results are categorized as follows:
  a. No Record: results that confirm there are no law violations reported by the
National Crime Information Center (NCIC).
  b. Criminal Record: results are charges returned on a Record of Arrests and
Prosecutions (RAP) sheet reported by NCIC. If the RAP Sheet does not have law
violations listed, this means the law violation has been sealed or expunged. An
approved exception is required to allow applicants to continue the process as stated in
paragraph G-6i(3) below.
  c. Unclassifiable: results that fingerprints were unreadable by NCIC; there is no
requirement to recapture fingerprints, as this will be completed at MEPS.

F-5. Live Scan results do not populate automatically; the results are uploaded only
when the RRNCO reenters Enroll Live Scan. The system will upload the results as in
one or more of the following:
   a. RZ Scan/Upload Documents – Live Scan Results.
   b. RZ Scan/Upload Documents – Live Scan Error.
   c. RZ Scan/Upload Documents – RAP Sheet.
   d. RZ Scan/Upload Documents – EBC Results.

Note: RAP Sheet can take up to 10 days to populate.

F-6. Recruiting and Retention Noncommissioned Officer (RRNCOs)
  a. The HRR Form 369 will be completed when the initial appointment is conducted
(to ensure the extremist questions are being asked initially) and be uploaded when
changed from a prospect to an applicant. The form is only required to be replaced if the
applicant has changed an answer. Fingerprints are only required to be submitted when
the applicant agrees to continue processing for enlistment.
  b. Do not submit fingerprints on prospects or applicants solely to ascertain if they
are morally qualified for enlistment. Further, RRNCOs will not fingerprint themselves,
family members (not processing for enlistment) or other RRNCOs. Warriors awaiting
shipment will not be fingerprinted for any reason unless directed by the ARNG-HRR-O-
ASO.
  c. RRNCOs will upload the required documents for place of birth, citizenship, Social
Security, and HRR 369 into the applicant’s record. Since all data entered in RZ should
have been confirmed using the source documents, this will reduce errors in the PII for
Live Scan submissions. The following is required to pass validation:
  (1) The Full Name, Social Security Number, Date of birth, Place of Birth Country,
Sex, Eye Color, Hair Color, Height, Weight, and Race are required to be entered in RZ.
  (2) Upload source documents for place of birth, citizenship, Social Security, and
HRR Form 369 in RZ.
  d. Do not change the data entered on the “Transaction Data” page unless subject
being fingerprinted is not an applicant; the RRNCO must obtain this information from the
State Security Manager. Example: Current Service Member.
  e. If fingerprints have been submitted and results have not been received, do not
resubmit the Live Scan file unless directed by the ARNG-HRR-O-ASO. If upon review

  90

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

of the submission it is discovered the file was sent with incorrect PII (i.e., SSN, POB,
DOB, etc.), contact the ARNG-HRR-O-ASO with the full name, PRID, and state what
the error was. Ensure source documents are uploaded into RZ for proof of correct PII.
Resubmission could cause a further delay in processing the fingerprints and additional
time to receive results.
  f. For LiveScan results that have not been returned after 72 hours, submit request
at NGB-ARNG-HRR-ASO-Live Scan under the "Request" tab, click NGB Live Scan
ETP/Request at top. To access the page, join the Teams Page using access code
“rnubnhl”.
  g. If results do not return to RZ, the users can access the LS Report in IKROme by
selecting "BI Zone", "Dashboards", “GCR – Processing”, and click “Live Scan”. Select
the appropriate RSID or search and enter the RSID or enter the applicant's SSN. Select
"Apply".
  h. The Cross Match ArcID User Guide is located on the ARNG IKROme Homepage
under ARISS System Resources.
  i. For fingerprints that are going to expire soon or recently expired, RRNCOs can
resubmit the file themselves; RRNCOs will not resubmit until the prints are older than 90
days. The RRNCO can search for the file ArcID by either the applicant name (Last,
First) or by searching for all their applicants with their username on the “Created by”
block. The format for the “Created by search is last name with first/ middle initial
(example: ThumWA). Select Resubmit from the dropdown and go through the prompts
to retransmit. Once the prints are older than 180 days old, they will no longer be visible
on the Live Scan site (WEBS). The recruiter will then need to complete a new
submission with the applicant.
  (1) If the LS report reads No Criminal Record under FBI Response those results
can be printed and scanned into EBC Results folder in EBC Results. This means the
applicant has no criminal record and may continue processing.
  (2) If the LS report indicates "record", “0/0/0” or “blank” under FBI Response and
a RAP Sheet is not in RZ, follow guidance in paragraph J-6h above.
  (3) If the LS report reads “RAP Sheet” under FBI Response, those results can be
printed and scanned into EBC Results folder in EBC Results. This means the applicant
has a criminal record. Applicant process may continue with the suitability exception if
an applicant has violations listed in RZ that would trigger a RAP Sheet (offenses level
200 or higher). Exceptions require a memorandum from the RRC or SGM to support
allowing the applicant to continue processing and verifying that the applicant is not
withholding any disqualifications. All police and court record checks will be uploaded in
RZ per 601-210, para 2-11a. The memorandum will also state the applicant may enlist
without RAP Sheet results. The memorandum will be uploaded into RZ under Other
Waiver Documents. If any previously undisclosed law violations and/or UCMJ actions
were returned on the RAP Sheet (except traffic), the Warrior will be discharged
regardless of disposition.

F-7. MEPS Guidance Counselors (GCs)
   a. Enter RZ and click “View Electronic Packet” to view the HRR Form 369 (EBC
Release) to ensure the form was uploaded prior to live scan results being posted. If the

  91

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

form is missing and/or was not uploaded prior to live scan case closing date, the MEPS
GC will submit an SR exception workflow stating the issue in the comments block. A
memorandum from the RRC, CSM, or OPS SGM explaining how the error occurred and
what corrective action was taken is required for continued processing
  b. Upload the memorandum into RZ under Other Waiver Document prior to
forwarding to the ARNG-HRR-O-ASO for consideration of continued processing.
  c. Compare the HRR Form 369 to the LS RAP Sheet. Applicants who failed to
disclose any offense(s), regardless of disposition, require police and court record
checks IAW AR 601-210, paragraph 2-11a and/or AOC, Chapter 2 except for level 100
offenses. To continue processing applicants who fail to disclose offenses, an approved
SR is required. Initiate SR exception workflow in RZ for review as follows:
  (1) When LS report is used as EBC results, compare the PRID from the LS report
with the PRID of the applicant's record during quality control (QC) procedures.
  (2) Fingerprints are valid for 120 days from the date posted on the Case Closing
Transmittal (CCT). GCs must be aware of the expiration dates of the FP’s as they
pertain to the background investigation.

F-8. State Operations Personnel
  a. Ensure that field requirements are being adhered to and only those applicants
who meet the FP criteria are allowed to process through the MEPS.
  b. If the live scan is processed and results post prior to HRR Form 369 being
uploaded, the State Waivers Analyst will review and action the suitability workflow.
  (1) An approved State level suitability workflow is required for Offense Level 100
& 200, regardless of disposition. Level 100 offenses require DMV History Report and
proof of payment uploaded in RZ. Level 200 offenses require police and court record
checks IAW AR 601-210, 2-11a and/or AOC, Chapter 2.
  (2) Level 300 and 400 offenses, regardless of disposition, require review and
approval from the ARNG-HRR-O-ASO. These offense levels require police and court
records IAW AR 601-210, 2-11a and/or AOC, Chapter 2. If the undisclosed offense(s)
is closed and does not require a conduct waiver, a control number may be provided to
allow the applicant to continue processing. A waiting period may be imposed based on
the seriousness of offenses withheld and if applicant requires a conduct waiver for the
undisclosed offenses to enlist.

Appendix G. Recruiting and Retention Section Chief Quality Control Checkpoint

chunks.title: FY26 AOC: Appendix G: Section Chief Quality Control Checkpoint
chunks.text:
G-1. The RRSC Quality Control (QC) checkpoint is designed to ensure RRNCOs and
RRSCs submit thoroughly reviewed processing packets to the MEPS GC. This function
improves processing efficiencies ensuring each applicant has the best experience while
processing for the ARNG. First-time success rates related to projection approvals are
associated with administrative errors and missing documentation when received by the
MEPS GC.

  92

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

G-2. The Initiate NCOIC Checkpoint action must be performed and approved before
any projection for enlistment. This includes those projected as a walk-in. Bypassing the
checkpoint with an Other Admin projection is not authorized to be converted to an
Accession projection. Department of the Army Civilian (DAC) GCs will be responsible
for reporting non-compliance to RRB Chains of Command and DAC MEPS Regional
Managers.

G-3. When unavailable, the RRSC may delegate up to two assistants to perform the
QC checkpoint action. States with an RRSC with large recruiting teams were
considered when determining the number of authorized delegates. The RRSC will use
discretion when assigning delegates and ensure maximum effectiveness of this
function. RRNCOs will not QC their own projections.

Appendix H. Non-MEPS Processing / Field Enlistment Option

chunks.title: FY26 AOC: Appendix H: Non-MEPS Processing / Field Enlistment Option
chunks.text:
H-1. Intent. To process applicants who, on the day of initial processing, required
additional screening and now meet all qualification standards without having to return to
MEPS to complete the enlistment process. Non-MEPS Processing (Outside MEPS
processing) can be completed virtually by using Teams between the GC and the
applicant or by a GC assigned to MEPS traveling to alternate locations to complete the
enlistment process.

H-2. This program requires collaboration between RRBs and MEPS GCs. Disputes
relating to the execution of this program will be settled by DACs with the assistance of
the NGB MEPS Regional Managers (RM). If states are not properly executing the
enlistment and accurately completing enlistment documents, NGB can suspend this
enlistment option.

H-3. Eligibility Requirements for Non-MEPS processing are listed below. The MEPS
GC will determine whether applicants meet non-MEPS processing enlistment option
criteria.
  a. Completion of aptitude testing (to include mandatory special purpose testing) IAW
UMR 611-1.
  b. Completion of accession medical examination requirements IAW UMR 40-1. HIV
and DAT Testing submitted IAW UMR 40-8.
  c. Must be physically qualified, and if applicable, has an approved medical waiver
IAW UMR 40-1.
  d. Applicants must have LiveScan results less than 100 days old.
  e. All NCOIC and GC QCs must be completed and in a GO Status prior to
processing.
  f. Execution of non-MEPS processing enlistment should only be conducted on
scheduled MEPS processing days (when MEPS is open). The only exception is if all
ROC, Incentives, and Vacancy overrides are already completed prior to the 24-hour QC

  93

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

by the MEPS GC. If not coordinated and approved by the MEPS GC, the “A” projection
will be cancelled and the applicant rescheduled.
  g. Non-MEPS processing enlistments will not be “walk-on” projections.
  h. Complete processing as outlined on HRR Form 102 and reference the example
packet posted on MS TEAMS in the Master Trainer files.
  i. MEPS GC will Enlist Confirm the record in REQUEST and immediately upload
required documents into US MIRS.
  j. The MEPS GC executing the contract is the only individual authorized to
complete the DD Form 4 and DD Form1966 series with the applicant and RRNCO.
RRNCOs or Operations NCOs will not complete these documents.
  k. Applicants enlisting into MOS 17C, 35N, 35P, or 35S must have telephonic
interview completed prior to the reservation being made. The applicant must be alone
and present in the recruiting office for the interview; a three-way call is not authorized.
  l. Applicants processing for any FSPC program covered in Appendix K will be
processed, enlisted, and shipped at MEPS.
  m. MEPS GCs will ensure the DD Form 93 and the DD Form 4 are reviewed for
accuracy prior to being uploaded into RZ.

Appendix I. Processing Requirements for MOSs 35M/35P

chunks.title: FY26 AOC: Appendix I: Processing Requirements for MOSs 35M/35P
chunks.text:
I-1. Must submit the 35M / 35P Request through MS TEAMS. Request MUST be in an
approved status prior to projecting for accession, no sooner than 48 hours from
approval. MS TEAMS: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/BQAXqA9mV5?origin=lprLink.

I-2. Intent. Authorizes the ARNG to utilize the current Department of the Army (DA)
ASVAB ST Score Pilot Program for enlisting into MOS 35M or 35P without a passing
score on the Defense Language Aptitude Battery (DLAB). Establishes procedures for
completing all 35M/35P reservations within WebREQUEST.

I-3. ST Line Score Pilot Program. The following DLAB/ASVAB changes are
implemented for ARNG applicants enlisting in 35M/35P:
  a. Applicants must achieve a ST line score of 110-119 for CAT I-III Initial Entry
Training (IET) languages taught at the Defense Language Institute (DEFLANG).
Applicants must score 120 or higher in ST to qualify for all languages CAT I-IV to enlist
and ship as either 35M/35P without taking the DLAB. If the ST line score does not meet
the requirement for unit authorized and desired language for the applicant, they may
take the DLAB (e.g., if the ST line score is 116 but unit authorized language is Korean
“KP” (CAT IV language) requiring ST line score of 120 or higher, the DLAB may be
administered). The DLAB may be administered upon arrival at DLI, solely for metrics
tracking purposes. Program participants will be allowed to choose any category (CAT)
(I-IV) language based on the following:
  (1) Authorized unit vacancies (non-excess positions, verified within REQUEST
3.0)

  94

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

  (2) Language(s) authorized for that unit (verified by a representative of the gaining
unit, NOT Automated Unit Vacancy System (AUVS)) manager or RRB Operations).
  (3) Based on the needs of the States and units, the applicant will have the choice
of language that meets the authorized vacancies and languages assigned to that unit.
  (4) The training path for 35M, pulled by the ROC, will be BCT-AIT with follow-on
language training at DEFLANG (if applicable and funding is available). The training
path for 35P will be BCT-DEFLANG-AIT. MEPS GC or State Operations NCO submit
the request as stated above prior to the applicant flooring at MEPS to verify unit
vacancy memorandum, vacancy, ASVAB, DLAB, DLPT scores (OPI for CASP), and
review applicant’s record for either Non-CASP or CASP enlistment options.
  b. Applicants with a ST line score less than 110 will be required to take and pass
the DLAB with a passing score based on the Category of language. If language
requirement is achieved via scoring high enough in the ST line score category, DLAB
projection should be cancelled. Exceptions are not authorized.
  c. Ensure the applicant meets MOS qualifications IAW DA PAM 611-21.

I-4. DLAB. Applicants enlisting as MOS 35M/35P utilizing the traditional DLAB method
(administered at MEPS) must have a passing score for the category of language being
considered.

I-5. Language Categories.
  a. CAT I – Must achieve a minimum DLAB score of 95
  b. CAT II – Must achieve a minimum DLAB score of 100
  c. CAT III – Must achieve a minimum DLAB score of 105
  d. CAT IV – Must achieve a minimum DLAB score of 110

I-6. Civilian Acquired Skills Program (CASP).
IAW DA PAM 611-21, Enlistment Option for native speakers of a language, (that is
authorized for the Unit accessing into, and the ARNG), other than English, will utilize
DLPT scores in lieu of DLAB to bypass DEFLANG for language training. Qualified
CASP applicants will attend BCT with follow-on AIT. Training paths will not include
DEFLANG in the REQUEST reservation letter or MEPS travel orders.
  a. The DLPT score is valid for 12 months from the date of test and must remain
valid through completion of AIT. Service Member (SM) enlisted as 35M/35P under the
CASP are required to return to the MEPS or nearest Education Center between 46 and
90 days of their scheduled ship date (if expected AIT graduation date is greater than 12
months from enlistment date). Exceptions for the 12-month policy may be submitted to
DA G-2 via suitability workflow through the ASO. Applicants must score 20 / 2 or higher
in both categories (listening/reading) on the DLPT to qualify for the CASP option
(documented on DA Form 330).
  b. If requesting 35M MOS as CASP, a request to take the Oral Proficiency Interview
(OPI) must be submitted through the DEFLANG system “OPI Authorization and
Reporting System (OARS)” after taking and passing the DLPT. To submit an OPI exam
request, the State must establish an account in OARS (instructions may be requested
or found in MS TEAMS). DEFLANG will work on the request and once approved will

  95

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

send notification of date, time, and location of applicant to take the OPI. This exam will
be done either on MS TEAMS or via a phone call. The location of the exam MUST be
an armory or education center where the applicant will have at least one hour without
any interruptions. The OPI interviewers are DEFLANG instructors in the specific
language being tested. Their time is extremely valuable (in between course instruction),
and any changes or updates to the testing period MUST be coordinated via OARS to
DEFLANG ASAP.
  c. If the DLPT is taken at an Education Center, the DA Form 330 will be uploaded
by the MEPS GC under “Core Documents” (DA Form 330 Oral Proficiency Interview
Score Sheet). Scores will then be entered/updated by the GC in GCRz under “Test
Scores” (Special Exam). The test type will be “DOD Standardized Test”. The
proficiency level for both DLPT and OPI scores (listening / reading / speaking) will be
entered as follows:
  (1) Memorized Proficiency = 0
  (2) No Proficiency = 0
  (3) Elementary Proficiency = 1
  (4) Elementary Proficiency Plus = 1+
  (5) Limited Working Proficiency = 2
  (6) Limited Working Proficiency Plus = 2
  (7) Gen Professional Prof Plus 40-ADV Professional Prof = 3+
  (8) General Professional Proficiency = 3
  (9) Adv Professional Prof Plus 50-FUNCTIONAL Native Prof = 4+
  (10) Functionally Native Proficiency = 5

I-7. Renegotiations.
Renegotiations will be evaluated using the whole person concept and on a case-by-
case basis. If the Warrior misses their original reserved ship date in WebREQUEST
due to the fault of the Warrior, a RENO will only be authorized into an MOS (NOT
35M/35P) that will have an expected AIT graduation date 24 months of the original Date
of Enlistment (DOE). The Warrior must be able to become DMOSQ within 24 months.

Appendix J. Processing Applicants Referred by members of the Army National

chunks.title: FY26 AOC: Appendix J: Processing Applicants Referred by ARNG Members
chunks.text:
Guard
  a. Per current Stripes for Buddies Program guidance, applicants referred by a
currently serving member of the ARNG must have the following remarks annotated by
the RRNCO on DD Form 1966: “I hereby state that I have been referred to join the
(State) ARNG by (referring Soldier’s Name), who is a drilling member of (Unit Name) on
(Date of Referral)”.
  b. RRNCOs will annotate in the MEPS Projection notes that this Soldier was

  c. RRSCs will verify that this remark is added on the DD Form 1966 in the RZ

Appendix K. Future Soldier Preparatory Course

chunks.title: FY26 AOC: Appendix K: Future Soldier Preparatory Course
chunks.text:
(Subsumes and Rescinds SMOM 24-019 and 23-023)

K-1. Recruiting Test Program Codes
   a. AM – Less than 2 percent (ARMS 2.0)
   b. A6 – Greater than 2 percent (ARMS 2.0 Expansion)
   c. T7 – Army Preparatory School (09M)

K-2. Program Descriptions and Requirements
Effective communication among Military Entrance Processing Station (MEPS) Guidance
Counselors (GCs), the REQUEST Operations Center (ROC), and Renegotiation
(RENO) NCOs is essential to ensure accurate training reservations. All reservations
must be made by the ARNG ROC; temporary reservations are not authorized.
   a. ARMS 2.0 (Program code AM). A performance-based option for applicants
exceeding body fat accession standards by no more than 2%.
  (1) Eligibility: Available to Non-Prior Service (NPS) applicants only (not
GNPS/PS). Not eligible for dual program enrollment (e.g. cannot combine with T7).
Must meet all enlistment criteria except body fat.
  (2) Qualifications:
  (a) Armed Forces Qualification Test (AFQT) score of 31 or higher.
  (b) For AFQT 31–49: Tailored Adaptive Personality Assessment System
(TAPAS) "Will Do" (WD) score of 100 or higher (no exceptions).
  (c) For AFQT 50+: No minimum TAPAS score.
  (3) Pre-Accession:
  (a) Body fat must be less than 2% above AR 40-501 standards.
  (b) Enlist under a 6x2 contract.
  (c) Split Training Option (STO) authorized.
  (d) Not authorized for Officer Producing Programs (09S, 09R, 09W), Foreign
Language Recruiting Initiative (FLRI; 09C), or English as a Second Language (ESL).
  (e) Major Misconduct Waiver(s) are not eligible.
  (4) Post-Accession: Must meet body fat standards within 1 year of enlistment
date; not subject to suspension of favorable personnel actions for body fat prior to the 1-
year mark.
   b. ARMS 2.0 Expansion (Program Code A6).
  (1) Eligibility: NPS only (not GNPS or PS). Not available for certain MOSs/CMFs
(see Table K-1). Not eligible for dual program enrollment (e.g. cannot combine with T7).
  (2) Qualifications:
  (a) Armed Forces Qualification Test (AFQT) score of 31 or higher.
  (b) Must be between 2.1 and 6% body fat composition.
  (c) For AFQT 31–49: Tailored Adaptive Personality Assessment System
(TAPAS) "Will Do" (WD) score of 100 or higher (no exceptions).
  (d) For AFQT 50+: No minimum TAPAS score.
  (3) Pre-Accession:
  (a) Applicants are not authorized to enlist into an MOS that requires training
beyond BCT and AIT.

  97

ARNG-HRH (RN 601)
SUBJECT: FY 26 Army National Guard Accession Options Criteria (PPOM 25-042)

  (b) Major Misconduct waiver(s) are not authorized.
  (c) Age ETPs are not authorized.
  (d) Changes or cancellations to ARMS 2.0 Expansion reservations will be
executed by the ROC. Send requests to FSPC Cancellation & RENO Request.
  (e) Split Option enlistments are NOT authorized.
  (f) Must enlist under a 6x2 contract.
  (g) Applicants are NOT authorized to enlist into Officer Producing Programs
(09S, 09R, and 09W).
  (h) Applicants must have a signed DA 5500/5501 by the Guidance Counselor
(GC) on the day of enlistment and prior to shipping for IET.
  (i) Applicants must be holding a primary vacancy for MOS.
  (4) Post-Accession:
  (a) Must be between 2.1 and 6% body fat composition on ship day to IET.
  (b) Warriors who no longer qualify for ARMS 2.0 Expansion (over 6%) may be
retained by the RRC for up to 12 months from the original contract date, provided they
meet initial entry body composition standards as outlined in 1d. prior to starting IET.
  (c) Warriors who enlisted under ARMS 2.0 Expansion and meet the 2% or
below body fat composition within 45 days of their scheduled FSPC start date can
RENO into a BCT/AIT seat.
  (d) Warriors who meet the 2% or below standards within the 44-day window
will arrive at the 120th RECBN, have their body fat validated, and will be inserted
directly into BCT start location from FSPC.

  c. Army Preparatory School (Program Code T7 – ASDP, 09M ONLY). The Army
Preparatory School (ASDP, 09M) empowers CAT IV applicants (AFQT 21–30) to
enhance their ASVAB scores, targeting a CAT IIIB or higher qualification to unlock MOS
opportunities. 09M enlistments are recorded as a CAT IV until retesting confirms a
higher category. All CAT IV accessions scoring between 21-30 will attend the
Academic Skills Development Enlistment Program (09M). Trainees discharged from
FSPC are ineligible for reentry into the ASDP. Reservations are secured against the
earliest available RECSTA date, with renegotiations permitted only for moral or medical
reasons. States, Recruiting and Retention NCOs (RRNCOs), and Guidance
Counselors (GCs) will not preassign or guarantee MOS selections prior to, during, or
after enlistment.
  (1) Eligibility:
  (a) NPS only (not GNPS or PS). Not eligible for dual program enrollment
(e.g. cannot combine with AM).
  (b) Requires a Tier 1 education credential (e.g., high school diploma).
  (c) Ineligible for applicants with major misconduct waivers or those enrolled in
English as a Second Language (ESL) programs.
  (d) Not authorized for Officer Producing Programs (09S, 09R, 09W) or
Foreign Language Recruiting Initiative (FLRI; 09C).
  (2) Qualifications:
  (a) Achieve an AFQT score of 21–30 on the ASVAB (Test Score Category
IV); no Exceptions to Policy (ETPs) permitted.
  (b) Valid MEPS physical examination, including Drug and Alcohol Test (DAT)
results and any approved medical waivers.
  (c) Completed Occupational Physical Assessment Test (OPAT), recorded
and uploaded to Recruiter Zone (RZ) prior to shipping.
  (d) Enlist under a 3x5 or 6x2 contract.
  (e) Pre-Accession:
  (f) Applicants must ship within the ROC-specified window to ensure program
alignment.
  (g) GCs will submit records to REQUEST, entering the Recruiting Test
Program Code "T7" on the Manage 680-ADP screen in RZ.
  (h) GCs will annotate the DD Form 1966 with: “I understand I will attend the
Future Soldier Preparatory Course (FSPC) to raise my Armed Forces Qualification Test
(AFQT) score. Upon successful improvement, I will be renegotiated into a Military
Occupational Specialty (MOS) for which I qualify, preferably within 50 miles of my Home
of Record (HOR). This MOS will align with the earliest available Basic Combat Training
(BCT) date and a valid vacancy per my State ARNG’s needs”. The Service Member
(SM) must initial this statement to confirm understanding.
  (i) Any changes or cancellations to T7 reservations will be processed by the
ROC via the TEAMS List FSPC Cancellation & RENO Request.
  (3) Post-Accession:
  (a) Trainees participate in a structured academic program for up to 90 days
from the class start date, focusing on ASVAB score improvement through intensive
instruction at Fort Jackson.
